detaileddescription.para: The flag is true if this DBG_VALUE is post-dominated by another DBG_VALUE of the same variable location. This is necessary to detect sequences such as: %0 = someinst DBG_VALUE %0, !123, !DIExpression() %1 = anotherinst DBG_VALUE %1, !123, !DIExpression() Where if %0 were to sink, the DBG_VAUE should not sink with it, as that would re-order assignments.

briefdescription.para: releaseMemory() - This member can be implemented by a pass if it wants to be able to release its memory when it is no longer needed.

detaileddescription.para: The default behavior of passes is to hold onto memory for the entire duration of their lifetime (which is the entire compile time). For pipelined passes, this is not a big deal because that memory gets recycled every time the pass is invoked on another program unit. For IP passes, it is more important to free memory when it is unused.
Optionally implement this function to release pass memory when it is no longer used.

briefdescription.para: hasStoreBetween - check if there is store betweeen straight line blocks From and To.
Postpone the splitting of the given critical edge (From, To).

detaileddescription.para: We do not split the edges on the fly. Indeed, this invalidates the dominance information and thus triggers a lot of updates of that information underneath. Instead, we postpone all the splits after each iteration of the main loop. That way, the information is at least valid for the lifetime of an iteration.

simplesect.para: True if the edge is marked as toSplit, false otherwise. False can be returned if, for instance, this is not profitable.

detaileddescription.para: This is easily rectified by forwarding the non-dominated debug uses to the copy source.
